what_works: Indian-centric topics (Cities, Powerful countries, 1962 War, Maritime boundary)
Hindi-English mixed titles (Hinglish) with high-intensity emojis
Custom thumbnails (Every video over 1,400 views has one)
Early morning IST publishing (6:00 AM - 9:00 AM)
Comparison or Ranking formats (Top 5, India vs China)

diagnosis.hook: The best videos use 'India' or 'Powerful' in the first 3 words. Weak videos use academic terms like 'Photosynthesis' or obscure names like 'Myeongnyang' which fail to stop the scroll.
diagnosis.buildup: Top videos maintain a 30-50 second duration. The 1962 War video (29s) shows that shorter, punchy historical facts perform better than longer 48s niche battles.
diagnosis.visuals: There is a 100% correlation between 'No Custom Thumbnail' and 'Under 100 views' in the recent data. Visual packaging is currently the biggest bottleneck.
diagnosis.titles_topics: The audience responds to national pride, geopolitical comparisons, and 'Top' lists. They ignore niche global history and basic science.
diagnosis.other: The channel median is 1,234, but the 'like_pct' on low-view videos is very high (12-15%), meaning the content is good, but the algorithm isn't finding an audience because the titles/thumbnails are too weak.

hook_rules: Must include a 'Shock' or 'Pride' element in the first 2 seconds
Use 'India' or 'Bharat' in the title for local relevance
Ask a question that can only be answered at the end (e.g., 'Bharat kis number par hai?')
Use numbers (Top 5, 3 Things, 1962) to provide structure
Start with a visual contradiction (e.g., a mud wall stopping an empire)
buildup_rules: Remove all 'Hello/Welcome' intros; dive straight into the fact
Use a 'Wait for the end' teaser if the fact is complex
visual_rules: Custom thumbnails are mandatory for every upload
Use high-contrast text on thumbnails (Yellow/Red on Black)
Always use 1-2 relevant emojis in the title to break up text
Ensure the main subject (e.g., a tank, a city, a cat) is large and clear
title_rules: Mix Hindi and English (Hinglish) to reach a wider demographic
Use ALL CAPS for power words (POWERFUL, DANGEROUS, MYSTERY)
Keep titles under 60 characters to avoid being cut off
Avoid academic or 'boring' words like 'Explained' or 'History of'
topic_rules: Unknown facts about famous Indian landmarks or figures
High-earning/Wealth-related facts (Cities, Business empires like TATA)
avoid: Purely English titles with no emojis
Niche global history that has no connection to India
Generic science topics that feel like school lessons
